newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Aznar signs pension deal with unions.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Aznar signs pension deal with unions.

text.p: Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar on Wednesday signed a deal with unions designed to guarantee the buying power and future payment of pensions.
The agreement, ratified by the cabinet on Friday, does not include employers but Labour Minister Javier Arenas said the door was open for them to join the accord.
"It isn't good that employers are setting themselves apart from the agreement," he told reporters at a press conference. "The system must count on businessmen in the future for its design."
Employers disagree with a clause in the pact which stipulates that their contributions must move in line with real wages within the next four years -- they are asking for seven years instead.
The agreement also ignores their requests that employers' social security contributions be reduced.
Unions say the deal is balanced and they consider it a show of solidarity because it consolidates the current pension system and guarantees the buying power of pensions in the future.

"It's a pact which benefits democracy, above all," said Antonio Gutierrez, secretary general of the Workers' Commissions (CCOO) union, one of the two biggest. "It's a milestone, in a way, since the beginning of democracy."
Union leaders have denied the pact was linked to the labour reform the government wants to finalise next year, which includes plans to make contracts more flexible.
